commits.title: Allow API-key accounts to use Daybreak in the TUI (#50433)
commits.message:
Allow API-key accounts to use Daybreak in the TUI (#50433)

## What changed

Allow accounts using an API key with the OpenAI provider to access `/daybreak` and Daybreak policy notices. Model availability and the connected server still determine program access.

Use the same eligibility checks for turn submission, continuation, and retries. For API-key accounts, send the selected `cyberAccessProgram` when Daybreak is enabled and omit it when Daybreak is off.

commits.title: Add keyboard copy selection to the owned transcript (#50434)
commits.message:
Add keyboard copy selection to the owned transcript (#50434)

## What changed

- Make `/copy` select the latest completed response directly in the owned transcript. Navigate user messages, code blocks, and blockquotes with arrow keys or `j`/`k`, use `g`/`G` to jump to the ends, and press Enter to copy or Escape to close.
- Highlight selected blocks and keep surrounding context visible during navigation and resizing. Preserve source payloads for code and quotes, including rendered Mermaid diagrams and fenced Markdown tables.
- Pause queued submissions until copy mode closes, and report clipboard results in the transcript footer.

## Testing

Add tests for copy routing, keyboard navigation, highlighting and resize behavior, source whitespace and line endings, clipboard completion, and queued-input resumption.

commits.title: Persist additional tool definitions in rollout history (#50435)
commits.message:
Persist additional tool definitions in rollout history (#50435)

## Why

`additional_tools` response items were excluded from rollout persistence, dropping their tool definitions from saved history.

## What changed

- Persist `additional_tools` items in both legacy and paginated history modes.
- Expose the variant in generated JSON schemas, TypeScript types, and Python models, with an optional `id`, a `role`, and arbitrary JSON tool definitions.

## Testing

Add a recorder round-trip test that verifies tool definitions survive recording and loading in both history modes without parse errors.

commits.message:
Add a CLI command to uninstall the legacy Windows sandbox (#50437)

## What changed

Add `codex sandbox uninstall` to remove machine-wide legacy Windows sandbox accounts and network rules with administrator privileges. Run cleanup without loading configuration, preserving Codex home, sandbox directories, and filesystem permissions. Reject the command on other platforms.

Keep commands after `--` forwarded to the sandbox, including `codex sandbox -- uninstall --help`.

## Testing

Add parsing coverage for the uninstall subcommand and command separator. Add an integration test verifying that help and invalid arguments work with malformed configuration and leave configuration and credentials unchanged.

commits.title: Support ordered response items in world-state context updates (#50441)
commits.message:
Support ordered response items in world-state context updates (#50441)

## Why

World-state sections could return only a single optional text fragment, with message separation controlled by the fragment itself. They could not contribute explicit `ResponseItem` values alongside instructions.

## What changed

- Let sections return ordered `WorldStateUpdate` values containing fragments or response items, with `Prefix`, `Standalone`, or `Mergeable` placement.
- Preserve explicit item boundaries when grouping context updates, and place prefix updates first when assembling initial context.
- Move standalone-message decisions from fragments to world-state updates and retain snapshot handling.

## Testing

Add tests for mixed fragment/item ordering, role and standalone boundaries, initial-context prefix placement, and snapshot restoration without repeated updates.

commits.message:
Preserve native USD amounts in thread usage responses (#50442)

## What changed

Add optional `native_usage_usd_micros` fields to thread usage totals and breakdown groups, and carry backend values through the client alongside existing credit and USD estimates. Missing or null native amounts remain `None`, while explicit zero amounts remain `Some(0)`.

## Testing

Add coverage for native totals and group amounts, mixed batches with legacy responses, and the distinction between missing, null, and zero native group amounts.

commits.title: Stabilize paused-time code-mode service tests (#50443)
commits.message:
Stabilize paused-time code-mode service tests (#50443)

## Why

Tokio's paused clock can auto-advance while tests await the V8 thread. The service tests need explicit control over time when checking yield limits and grace periods.

## What changed

- Hold virtual time with a blocking-task guard that is released when dropped.
- Replace bounded polling loops with tool-start notifications and direct awaits of response tasks.
- Return an error from the test helper if the cell closes before a nested tool starts.

## Testing

Add tests covering tool-start acknowledgement when a cell throws or is terminated before invoking a nested tool, including assertions on the resulting cell responses.

commits.message:
Assert that only direct tool calls emit timing events (#50445)

## What changed

Strengthen `tool_call_timing_guard_ignores_code_mode_source` to capture tracing output and assert that direct and nested code-mode calls together emit exactly one `codex.tool_call` event. Disable ANSI formatting and keep callsite interest independent of untraced parallel test threads.

commits.message:
Bundle rollout attachments into a gzip tar archive (#50446)

## What changed

- Combine file-backed rollouts and buffered rollout prefixes into `rollouts.tar.gz`, keeping diagnostics as separate attachments.
- Bound the archive and its upload envelope by the existing size limit, skip invalid or duplicate archive filenames, and fall back to individual rollout attachments if archiving fails.
- Add `rollout_archive_filename` to the report thread index so rollout filenames identify archive entries or fallback attachments.

Add an upload test that extracts the archive and verifies the filenames and contents of both a compressed file-backed rollout and a buffered rollout. Update the thread index test to check the archive filename.

commits.message:
Remove the provider capability gate for tool namespaces (#50447)

## What changed

- Remove `namespace_tools` from `ProviderCapabilities` and `namespaceTools` from `ModelProviderCapabilitiesReadResponse`, updating generated schemas and SDK types.
- Preserve tool namespaces and configured collaboration tool namespaces without a provider capability check, and always use Responses Lite tool serialization for Responses Lite requests.

commits.message:
Measure rollout persistence size reductions (#50454)

## What changed

- Record original and persisted item sizes in `codex.rollout.persistence.item_bytes_v2`, distinguished by stage, and record positive size reductions in `codex.rollout.persistence.bytes_removed`. Count the full original size as removed for dropped items.
- Use explicit histogram boundaries from 1 KiB to 64 MiB for item sizes, bytes removed, and `codex.rollout.persistence.turn_bytes_v2`. Larger values remain represented in the overflow bucket and histogram sum.

commits.title: Truncate oversized MCP results in paginated thread history (#50458)
commits.message:
Truncate oversized MCP results in paginated thread history (#50458)

## Why

Paginated thread history can persist large MCP results in completed tool-call items. Bound these stored results to avoid retaining multi-megabyte payloads.

## What changed

Apply a 64 KiB preview budget when persisting oversized MCP results in paginated history. Replace the result with a truncated text preview of its serialized JSON, preserving `is_error` and clearing `structuredContent` and `_meta`. Leave small results unchanged.

Share the truncation helper with the existing MCP tool-call event path.

## Testing

Add helper tests for unchanged small results and oversized results with structured content and metadata. Add a thread-history test verifying that persisted MCP results contain a bounded preview with the beginning, end, and truncation marker while preserving tool arguments.

commits.title: Add capability overrides for custom model providers (#50459)
commits.message:
Add capability overrides for custom model providers (#50459)

## What changed

Allow Responses-compatible providers to configure live web access and remote compaction under `model_providers.<id>.capabilities`:

```toml
[model_providers.custom.capabilities]
external_web_access = false
remote_compaction = "v2"
```

`external_web_access = false` keeps hosted web search from accessing the live web. `remote_compaction` accepts `v2` to send `compaction_trigger` items through the Responses endpoint, or `unsupported` to use local compaction. Omitted capabilities retain existing provider defaults.

## Testing

Add unit coverage for preserving unspecified defaults and a request-snapshot scenario verifying cached web search and V2 compaction for a custom provider.

commits.title: Populate thread previews from delegated task inputs (#50462)
commits.message:
Populate thread previews from delegated task inputs (#50462)

## Why

Delegated turns can begin without a user message, leaving threads without a task preview. Populate the preview from delegated input so these threads are discoverable before a user follow-up.

## What changed

- Extract previews from completed `create_thread` and `send_message_to_thread` outputs in the `codex_app` and `codex_tui` namespaces.
- Unwrap recognized `<codex_delegation>` inputs and decode their escaped task text for display, preserving model content. Keep plain or unrecognized wrappers as text and ignore blank inputs.
- Fill missing previews in state metadata extraction and live thread metadata updates without replacing existing previews or setting the title or `first_user_message`.

## Testing

Add tests for delegation decoding and tool filtering, preview-only metadata updates, preservation of later user-message metadata, and database listing before a user follow-up in both legacy and paginated history modes.

commits.title: Retry registry authentication outages and jitter executor reconnects (#50465)
commits.message:
Retry registry authentication outages and jitter executor reconnects (#50465)

## Why

Remote executors need to recover from confirmed authentication-service outages and spread reconnect attempts after a shared outage. Registration retries must remain limited to confirmed failures before a write, since replaying an ambiguous request can replace a newer registration.

## What changed

- Retry registry responses with HTTP 502 and `authentication_service_unavailable`, alongside the existing HTTP 503 `registration_conflict` retries.
- Accept structured registry errors in `detail`, keeping the canonical `error` authoritative when both are present.
- Randomize reconnect delays between half and all of the current exponential backoff, retaining the 30-second cap.

## Testing

Add coverage for reconnect jitter bounds, authentication-outage retry cancellation, error-envelope precedence, and preservation of Noise identity and initialized sessions across retries. Make the HTTP-header helper cleanup test wait for the helper PID before cancellation and verify process termination when the provider is dropped.

commits.title: Copy transcript selections as literal text while preserving rich HTML (#50467)
commits.message:
Copy transcript selections as literal text while preserving rich HTML (#50467)

## Why

Copying rendered transcript selections added Markdown formatting and escapes to the plain-text clipboard payload. Selecting bold text such as `hello` could paste as `**hello**`.

## What changed

Separate the literal selection text from the Markdown source used to render clipboard HTML. Plain-text copies omit inline formatting delimiters, added code fences, and Markdown escapes while retaining list and table structure. Rich-text pastes continue to preserve formatting through HTML.

## Testing

Update clipboard and transcript selection tests to verify literal text alongside rich HTML, including lists, inline code, paths with Markdown punctuation, hard breaks, streamed code blocks, and tables across layout widths.

commits.title: Account for JSON overhead when truncating MCP tool results (#50470)
commits.message:
Account for JSON overhead when truncating MCP tool results (#50470)

## Why

Truncating the preview alone can leave the serialized MCP tool result above its byte budget because JSON escaping and the result wrapper add bytes.

## What changed

Measure the complete serialized replacement and progressively reduce the preview budget until the result fits or the preview is empty.

## Testing

Strengthen the regression test with quotes, backslashes, and newlines. Assert that the serialized result fits within the 1,024-byte budget and that truncating it again returns the existing result unchanged.

commits.title: Enable Ultrafast service tiers for Amazon Bedrock Astra models (#50472)
commits.message:
Enable Ultrafast service tiers for Amazon Bedrock Astra models (#50472)

## Why

Bedrock catalogs cleared all service-tier metadata, and requests omitted every selected tier. This prevented users from selecting `ultrafast` or using tiers defined in custom catalogs.

## What changed

- Advertise `ultrafast` for `openai.gpt-6-astra` on Mantle and the `global.openai.gpt-6-astra` and `us.openai.gpt-6-astra` Runtime variants, while retaining the implicit default tier unless users select otherwise.
- Preserve custom catalog speed tiers, service-tier definitions, and defaults while continuing to normalize Bedrock web search compatibility.
- Send selected service tiers only when the Bedrock model advertises them, including `flex`.

## Testing

Add coverage for `model/list` tier discovery, custom catalog preservation, configured and per-turn HTTP request tiers, and TUI slash-command selection, toggling, and model switching.

commits.message:
Skip managed config loading for registered Windows sandbox refreshes (#50480)

## Why

Registration-only refreshes retain the existing sandbox, so package maintenance should not require another cloud-policy fetch.

## What changed

Skip managed configuration loading when a provisioning request has both `registered_core` and `refresh_only` set. The registered-runtime transaction still checks the existing owner, accounts, and unchanged settings under the setup lock. Other provisioning requests continue to enforce managed policy.

## Testing

commits.title: Include installer stderr in daemon update failures (#50499)
commits.message:
Include installer stderr in daemon update failures (#50499)

## Why

Daemon updates discard installer stderr, leaving failed installs with only an exit status and no installer diagnostics.

## What changed

Capture the last 2 KiB of installer stderr and append it to errors when the installer exits unsuccessfully. Drain stderr concurrently and wait at most one second after failure so subprocesses holding the pipe open cannot delay error reporting indefinitely. Keep captured details within the manual update response limit, and configure PowerShell output as UTF-8 to preserve non-ASCII diagnostics.

## Testing

Add coverage for stderr tail truncation, bounded draining when a subprocess keeps stderr open, and manual update responses containing heavily escaped diagnostics. Extend the Windows installer test to check non-ASCII error text.

Use Enter to accept transcript Find results and Escape to cancel (#50503)

## Why

Accepting a Find result must not let a held `Enter` submit the composer draft, including when terminals report repeated keys as fresh presses.

## What changed

- Make `Enter` accept the displayed result for reading, while `Ctrl+P` and `Ctrl+N` navigate older and newer matches.
- Make `Escape` cancel query editing and restore the pre-search presentation; after acceptance, it returns to the latest transcript content.
- Consume unmodified `Enter` while reading a result, but let modified `Enter` reach configured composer bindings.
- Update footer hints to show acceptance, cancellation, and the active Find state.

## Testing

Extend input-routing coverage for repeated `Enter` presses and modified composer bindings. Update search tests and footer snapshots for acceptance, cancellation, and result navigation.

commits.title: Keep Command Center selection adjacent after task removal (#50505)
commits.message:
Keep Command Center selection adjacent after task removal (#50505)

## Why

Archiving or deleting the selected task could make Command Center selection jump to the current task instead of a neighboring task in the displayed list.

## What changed

Choose the next surviving task in displayed order before removing tasks, falling back to the previous task when needed. Apply this selection behavior to archive, delete, and hide actions, respecting filtering and grouping.

Preserve the pending selection across view rebuilds, batched removals, and duplicate server notifications. Allow selection to fall back when a rename target disappears while retaining the existing notice about its unsubmitted title.

## Testing

Add regression tests and snapshots for archive/delete selection across project, status, and model grouping, with and without filtering. Cover removal of the attached task, external removal notifications, removal of a pending successor, repeated repaints, and an empty task list. Update the disappeared-rename-target snapshot to verify that the remaining selection is preserved.

commits.title: Record Windows sandbox service stop diagnostics (#50507)
commits.message:
Record Windows sandbox service stop diagnostics (#50507)

## What changed

Persist the service's last reported lifecycle reason and numeric HRESULT in the existing service registry key. Distinguish requested stops, shutdown, owner removal, startup failure, broker failure, and interrupted registration, and reset the record on startup. Recording is best-effort and does not affect the service lifecycle.

Emit `codex.windows_sandbox.service_stopped` when a provisioning client observes a stopped service, including the recorded reason, HRESULT, and Windows service exit codes. Recheck the service status and registry record before emitting to avoid pairing inconsistent evidence during a concurrent restart. The metric counts observations, not unique outages; the recorded reason is advisory.

Update the cached service status only after `SetServiceStatus` succeeds. Extract diagnostic error codes from typed errors without collecting error text or user data.

## Testing

Add a test covering Win32-to-HRESULT conversion, preservation of Windows HRESULTs through error context, and a zero fallback for untyped error text.

Reject unknown TUI keys in strict config validation (#50525)

## Why

Flattened notification settings prevent `serde_ignored` from detecting unknown keys in `[tui]`, allowing them to pass `--strict-config` validation.

commits.message:
Use issuing-step context for Guardian MCP elicitation reviews (#51067)

## Why

MCP elicitation reviews used turn-start context, which could omit remote environments that became ready before the tool invocation and use stale environment permissions.

## What changed

Capture the issuing step's Guardian review context with each live MCP invocation and reuse it for elicitation reviews. Fall back to turn context when no matching live invocation is available, and preserve the captured context for in-flight actions.

## Testing

Extend the deferred-executor regression test to cover MCP elicitations, checking that Guardian receives the newly ready remote environment and its denied paths, excludes stale local denied paths, and returns the denial to the parent model.

commits.title: Preserve trusted-tool context in Guardian Decisions requests (#51070)
commits.message:
Preserve trusted-tool context in Guardian Decisions requests (#51070)

## Why

The Decisions adapter rejected developer messages, including host-annotated trusted-tool context. Requests containing that context could not be classified.

## What changed

Append developer text annotated with `TrustedTool::KIND` to the classification rubric, preserving its authority while keeping user evidence in the input messages. Accept only a single text part with a single matching annotation; continue rejecting other developer messages and unsupported evidence.

## Testing

Add a regression test covering trusted-tool context alongside untrusted user text, plus rejection of incorrect roles, missing or mismatched annotations, multiple annotations or content parts, and image content.

commits.message:

## Why

Remote executors need to recover from confirmed authentication-service outages and spread reconnect attempts after a shared outage. Registration retries must remain limited to confirmed failures before a write, since replaying an ambiguous request can replace a newer registration.

## What changed

- Retry registry responses with HTTP 502 and `authentication_service_unavailable`, alongside the existing HTTP 503 `registration_conflict` retries.
- Accept structured registry errors in `detail`, keeping the canonical `error` authoritative when both are present.
- Randomize reconnect delays between half and all of the current exponential backoff, retaining the 30-second cap.

## Testing

Add coverage for reconnect jitter bounds, authentication-outage retry cancellation, error-envelope precedence, and preservation of Noise identity and initialized sessions across retries. ## Why

Daemon updates discard installer stderr, leaving failed installs with only an exit status and no installer diagnostics.

## What changed

Capture the last 2 KiB of installer stderr and append it to errors when the installer exits unsuccessfully. Keep captured details within the manual update response limit, and configure PowerShell output as UTF-8 to preserve non-ASCII diagnostics.

commits.title: Record Windows sandbox service stop diagnostics (#50507)
commits.message:
Record Windows sandbox service stop diagnostics (#50507)

## What changed

Persist the service's last reported lifecycle reason and numeric HRESULT in the existing service registry key. Distinguish requested stops, shutdown, owner removal, startup failure, broker failure, and interrupted registration, and reset the record on startup. Recording is best-effort and does not affect the service lifecycle.

Emit `codex.windows_sandbox.service_stopped` when a provisioning client observes a stopped service, including the recorded reason, HRESULT, and Windows service exit codes. Recheck the service status and registry record before emitting to avoid pairing inconsistent evidence during a concurrent restart. The metric counts observations, not unique outages; the recorded reason is advisory.

Add the disabled-by-default `code_mode_only_strict_3p_tools` feature, applied only when the effective model tool mode is Code Mode Only.

- Preserve disabled, app-only, policy-denied, and over-budget tool restrictions. Keep built-in tool exposure unchanged, including when a dynamic tool has the same name.

Add unit and integration coverage for exposure overrides, effective model modes, tool eligibility, and app discovery and dispatch. Add an MCP refresh scenario that verifies the eager tool prefix stays unchanged as tools are added, replaced, and removed while `exec` tracks the current catalog.

commits.title: Decode Windows Terminal's mapped Shift+Enter sequence (#50720)
commits.message:
Decode Windows Terminal's mapped Shift+Enter sequence (#50720)

## Why

Windows Terminal's `sendInput` mapping delivers `ESC[13;2u` as individual console key events. Decode it as `Shift+Enter` so the mapping inserts a newline in the composer.

## What changed

- Wrap the Windows event stream with a decoder for the complete Escape-prefixed sequence, including interleaved key releases.
- Use a fixed 50 ms deadline for partial sequences and replay incomplete or mismatched input unchanged. Preserve literal text, paste events, and native key events.
- Update the `crossterm` revision and dependency lockfiles.

## Testing

Add tests for repeated and fragmented mappings, deadline handling, unchanged input, error and end-of-stream replay, and composer newline rendering with a snapshot.

commits.message:
Use server model defaults for connected TUI fresh starts (#50913)

## Why

Fresh starts connected to an app server can bootstrap with stale client model settings before reading the server configuration. An empty model catalog can also prevent startup even when managed new-thread defaults provide a model.

## What changed

- Read server configuration before model bootstrap for fresh starts using a local daemon or remote server without an explicit profile.
- Preserve explicit model and reasoning-effort overrides, clear implicit client settings when `config/read` is unsupported, and allow managed new-thread defaults to supply a model when the catalog is empty.
- Use the launch directory for local daemon configuration reads and the server directory for remote reads.

## Testing

Update startup-default tests to cover managed model selection with an empty catalog. Strengthen the reconnect test with a stale client model and an assertion that `config/read` uses the server directory.

commits.title: Recover malformed Windows deny-read ACL state safely (#50940)
commits.message:
Recover malformed Windows deny-read ACL state safely (#50940)

## Why

Malformed `deny_read_acl_state.json` previously caused deny-read ACL reconciliation to fail. Recovery must restore bookkeeping without removing unknown existing restrictions or modifying a linked file's contents.

## What changed

- Retry malformed reads for up to two seconds, then rebuild bookkeeping only after excluding active writers and successfully applying current deny-read ACLs. Preserve unknown historical denies and continue propagating I/O errors.
- Validate the opened state file before reading or writing, rejecting reparse points and files with multiple hard links.
- Write state in place without truncating before validation, preserving file identity and permissions. Retry sharing violations during writes while preventing replacement through delete access.

## Testing

Add Windows tests for corrupt-state recovery, linked-file rejection, concurrent writer and delete-handle behavior, file identity and ACL preservation, and subsequent permission-profile changes. Extend the elevated sandbox integration test to verify that denied reads remain blocked after recovery while allowed writes and deletes succeed.

commits.title: Gate stable environment tool exposure behind a feature flag (#50962)
commits.message:
Gate stable environment tool exposure behind a feature flag (#50962)

## What changed

Add the default-off `stable_environment_tools` feature flag. When enabled, advertise environment-backed tools before an executor is ready, keep environment selectors stable as readiness changes, and include the `shell` and `login` parameters. Execution still requires a usable environment and its policy.

When disabled, expose environment-backed tools only when a usable environment exists, derive selectors from usable environments, and condition shell parameters on the execution configuration. Restore tool-specific unavailable-environment errors and skip the environment readiness check for `write_stdin`.

## Testing

Parameterize the empty-environment tool availability test for both flag states, check that commands require a ready transport by default, and explicitly opt tests that rely on stable tool exposure into the feature.

## Why

MCP elicitation reviews used turn-start context, which could omit remote environments that became ready before the tool invocation and use stale environment permissions.

Capture the issuing step's Guardian review context with each live MCP invocation and reuse it for elicitation reviews. Fall back to turn context when no matching live invocation is available, and preserve the captured context for in-flight actions.

commits.message:
Preserve trusted-tool context in Guardian Decisions requests (#51070)

## Why

The Decisions adapter rejected developer messages, including host-annotated trusted-tool context. Requests containing that context could not be classified.

## What changed

Append developer text annotated with `TrustedTool::KIND` to the classification rubric, preserving its authority while keeping user evidence in the input messages. Accept only a single text part with a single matching annotation; continue rejecting other developer messages and unsupported evidence.

## Testing

Add a regression test covering trusted-tool context alongside untrusted user text, plus rejection of incorrect roles, missing or mismatched annotations, multiple annotations or content parts, and image content.
